summary:
PLANETDLE is an interactive, Wordle-inspired astronomy game designed to make space education engaging, accessible, and part of everyday life. In a world where short-form entertainment dominates our attention, we wanted to transform a few minutes of screen time into a meaningful learning experience.
Players are challenged to identify a mystery celestial object in six attempts by comparing scientific characteristics such as size, temperature, atmosphere, and orbital relationships. The game also features an animated 3D solar system, realistic planetary models, NASA imagery, and educational facts that encourage curiosity and exploration.
PLANETDLE addresses the challenge of making space education more interactive by combining scientific reasoning with short, rewarding gameplay. Through one daily challenge, our goal is to encourage consistent learning without overwhelming users.
We believe that learning about space shouldn't require hours of studying. Sometimes, a few minutes of curiosity can spark a lifelong interest in science.
details:
PLANETDLE transforms astronomy education into an interactive daily guessing game. Players have six attempts to identify a mystery celestial object from 21 possible answers, including planets, moons, dwarf planets, asteroids, and comets.

After each guess, the game provides color-coded feedback comparing six scientific properties: object type, orbital relationship, size, atmosphere, temperature, and diameter. This encourages players to analyze information, make comparisons, and improve their guesses through logical reasoning.

The website also features an interactive 3D solar system with orbiting celestial objects, realistic planetary textures, scientific information, and images retrieved through NASA's Image and Video Library API.

Problem and Motivation

Many people are accustomed to consuming short-form content, making lengthy educational experiences less appealing to some audiences. Instead of trying to change how people consume content, we designed an educational experience that fits into their daily routines.

PLANETDLE addresses this by using short gameplay sessions and a daily challenge to make astronomy education more approachable, engaging, and enjoyable.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our project aims to encourage curiosity about space, strengthen scientific reasoning, and make astronomy more accessible to students and beginners.

By presenting scientific information through interactive gameplay, we hope to motivate users to learn a little more about the solar system each day and gradually develop a lasting interest in astronomy and space exploration.

Technologies and Development

We developed PLANETDLE using Python and Flask for backend development, game logic, and server communication. HTML, CSS, and JavaScript power the interactive user interface, gameplay mechanics, and animations.

WebGL-based 3D rendering enables interactive planetary models and solar system visualization, while NASA's Image and Video Library API provides access to authentic space imagery. We also incorporated scientific planetary texture assets to create realistic representations of celestial objects.

GitHub was used for source code hosting and version control, while Render was used to deploy the website online.

The project is entirely software-based and runs directly in a web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

Rather than building another astronomy encyclopedia or traditional educational game, we combined the familiar mechanics of Wordle with scientific reasoning and visual exploration.

The daily challenge encourages short, consistent engagement, while the interactive solar system allows players to explore the celestial objects they encounter during gameplay.

Our approach brings together entertainment, education, and curiosity in a single accessible experience.

Design Considerations

Throughout development, we prioritized accessibility, simplicity, scientific accuracy, performance, and user engagement. We designed the interface to be understandable for users regardless of their existing astronomy knowledge, while keeping gameplay intuitive and feedback informative.

We also considered performance and accessibility to ensure that the experience remains usable across different devices and browsers.
